subject.title: memory_search: chokidar file watcher silently stops delivering events, index goes stale

question: Should unconfigured memory search get a default periodic fallback sync, or should interval sync remain opt-in while watcher health is improved another way?
rationale: Current main has no default fallback when memory watcher events are missed, but changing the default interval changes background indexing behavior for existing users.

options.title: Accept default periodic fallback
options.body: Land a repaired version of the linked PR with source-scoped dirty marking, docs, tests, and upgrade proof for the background rescan behavior.

options.title: Keep interval opt-in
options.body: Leave intervalMinutes at 0 by default and document or surface intervalMinutes: 30 as the explicit workaround while improving watcher health separately.

options.title: Use a different health-check path
options.body: Reject the default interval change and instead require a watcher liveness or doctor recovery design before closing this issue.

recommendation.title: Accept default periodic fallback
recommendation.body: Land a repaired version of the linked PR with source-scoped dirty marking, docs, tests, and upgrade proof for the background rescan behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest recent history on the memory manager, stale-index, and SQLite-backed memory index paths affected by the decision.
